title: Aurora
subtitle: Recurring-campaign setup dropped from three clicks to one. I put an AI writer inside the email canvas, and brought Aurora in line with the rest of the Helio suite.

overview.headline: Project Overview
overview.tldr: I cut campaign setup from three clicks to one, and put an AI writer inside the email canvas so writers stopped pasting from ChatGPT. Aurora is a B2B marketing product in Europe, acquired by Helio. I used their platform rebuild to fix a dense, engineer-led UI and shipped a Figma design system that brought Aurora in line with the suite.
overview.intro: Aurora is a B2B marketing product for large European enterprises. Helio bought it to round out their suite while rebuilding the technical foundations. That gave me a window: bring Aurora in line with Helio's design language while the engineers rebuilt the plumbing. Names are stand-ins; the real client is under NDA.
overview.intro2: The old product worked, but it was engineer-built. Dense, inconsistent, visually fragmented. Marketers fought cluttered panels to schedule a recurring campaign. Writers had no AI in the composer, so they wrote in ChatGPT and pasted back.
overview.contextBody: The rebuild was the moment to reduce clutter, simplify the flows, and bring the look in line with the rest of Helio.

primaryUsers.label: Campaign Managers
primaryUsers.desc: Marketers who build and ship recurring campaigns. Need setup to be fast, and results easy to prove.

primaryUsers.label: Marketing Ops Leads
primaryUsers.desc: Own the rules and audit trail across brand portfolios. Need consistency across every campaign.

primaryUsers.label: Copywriters
primaryUsers.desc: Producing on-brand copy. Lean on the in-canvas AI writer to beat the blank page.

problem.headline: The Problem
problem.quote: I spend more time setting up the schedule than writing the actual campaign. By the time it's set, I've lost the creative momentum.
problem.quoteAttribution: Senior CRM Manager, hospitality client (discovery interview, week 2)

challenges.d: Nothing matched. Customers were already opening tickets about confusing flows, and it got worse once Helio rolled out a suite-wide look Aurora didn't share.
The tools for the most important use cases were still shallow. Customers kept asking for the depth to run nuanced campaigns, and the old UI could not express it.
The same task had a different flow and a different look depending on where you started. Every new feature drifted a little further from the last. That wore down trust.

problem.scopeIntro: I drew a hard box around the work. Two surfaces caused most of the pain: recurring-campaign setup and the email composer. I built a reusable design system alongside them.
inScope: Email composer with in-canvas Helio AI
Reusable design system aligned with Helio's brand
outOfScope: Full re-architecture of the platform (the engineering team owned this)
problem.hypothesis: Simplify the two most-used surfaces and match the Helio look: setup speeds up, writers get help where they write, and the product feels like one suite.
hypothesisBullets: Fewer clicks to set up a recurring campaign
AI writing help inside the canvas, not a separate tab
One visual language shared with Helio
problem.keyInsight: The old flow made writers switch modes just to schedule. Meeting them in one place, schedule, write, ship, was the real unlock.

research.headline: Research
research.auditTitle: UX audit of the old product
research.auditIntro: I walked every screen and scored them against one bar: could a first-time marketer ship a campaign without asking for help? Mostly no. Three problems repeated.

auditFindings.d: The interface pushed scheduling and rules to the front and left the actual message for last. Writers had to plan the machinery before they wrote a word.
Similar controls looked different on every page. That is not a look problem, it is a learning problem.
The AI writer sat on a different page. Writers copied into ChatGPT and pasted back, losing formatting on the way.

heuristics.d: Same controls, different behavior on different pages.
Feedback after a save or send was vague or delayed.
Jargon and internal names leaked into the UI.

stakeholders.quote: The rebuild is the window. If we do not simplify now, we ship the old UI in new paint.
I do not want more features. I want to ship one campaign in half the time.

findings.d: Everyone talked about features, but the number that mattered was how long a recurring campaign took to leave the door.
"Suggest me a subject line" beat "write the email for me" every time. AI as an assistant, not a replacement.

insights.headline: Insights

personas.name: Priya
frustrations: Too many clicks to set the schedule

personas.name: Marco
goals: Write in one place, ship from that place

designGoals.d: Schedule and write in the same canvas. No jumping between pages.
Cut steps in recurring setup without cutting the depth marketers need.
Suggestions the writer can accept, edit, or dismiss. Never automatic.

insights.keyInsight: Marketers do not need a smarter tool. They need a faster one that shares a language with the rest of their day.

design.headline: The Design
design.sketchesIntro: I started on paper. Fast, cheap, honest. Two directions for the recurring flow, two for where AI lives in the composer.

sketches.title: Recurring setup, sketched
sketches.desc: First pass: one page, one flow. Schedule and content on the same canvas instead of a wizard.

sketches.title: AI in the canvas, sketched
sketches.desc: The writer stays in the composer. AI shows up as a menu inside the block they are working on.

design.wireframesIntro: Rough layouts to check the flow before applying any look. Every element has a job, and every job has a home.

wireframes.title: Journey type
wireframes.desc: Pick the kind of recurring campaign in one step. The old flow buried this three levels deep.

wireframes.title: Weekly schedule
wireframes.desc: The schedule you set is the schedule you see. No hidden rules, no separate preview screen.

wireframes.title: Helio quick actions
wireframes.desc: One-tap AI actions inside the block the writer is editing.

wireframes.title: Subject variations
wireframes.desc: AI-drafted alternatives for the subject line, sitting where you set the subject.

design.finalIntro: Finished screens with the Helio look. Fewer steps, one canvas for schedule and content, and the AI writer right where you type.

finalScreens.title: Journey type, basic fields
finalScreens.desc: One screen to pick the kind of recurring campaign. The old flow needed three.

finalScreens.title: Journey type, all fields
finalScreens.desc: Depth is there when you need it. Hidden when you do not.

finalScreens.title: Content tab
finalScreens.desc: Pick or draft the email in the same view where you set the schedule.

finalScreens.title: Properties, weekly
finalScreens.desc: One page for the rules and the schedule. No separate preview.

finalScreens.title: Properties, monthly
finalScreens.desc: Same layout, monthly cadence. Learn one, read them all.

finalScreens.title: Properties, custom
finalScreens.desc: Custom cadences without leaving the page.

finalScreens.title: Composer, empty state
finalScreens.desc: AI is right where the writer starts. No new page, no context switch.

finalScreens.title: Text block selected
finalScreens.desc: Selecting a block surfaces the tools that apply to it. Nothing else moves.

finalScreens.title: "Make it shorter"
finalScreens.desc: One-tap rewrites for common asks. The writer stays in charge.

finalScreens.title: AI menu in canvas
finalScreens.desc: The full AI menu opens inside the block. No new page, no lost formatting.

finalScreens.title: Blocks library
finalScreens.desc: Every block reused across the suite lives here. One library, one language.

designSystem.headline: Design System
designSystem.intro: Alongside the two flows, I built the Aurora design system in Figma: tokens, components, patterns aligned with Helio. Shipped 52 components, picked up by three other Helio products, cut new-screen build time in half.
designSystem.systemOutcomes: Shipped 52 components. Reused by three other Helio products with zero new design work.
designSystem.crossProduct: The system made cross-team work easy for the first time. Designers on other Helio products started pulling from Aurora tokens instead of building their own.

validation.headline: Iterative Testing
validation.intro: Five rounds, 20+ participants. Each round narrowed the changes; by round four we were fixing labels, not layouts.

rounds.d: Do marketers understand the one-page flow? Yes, and they asked why the old product did not work this way.
Timed the setup. Six clicks dropped to two, then to one after we merged the schedule and content step.
Writers wanted control over tone and length. Added "make shorter", "more formal", and "rewrite" as one-tap actions.
Labels rewritten to match how marketers actually talk about their work. "Cadence" out, "how often" in.
Walked the build team through every screen. Every screen tied to a requirement in Jira.

validation.outcome: Setup dropped 3:1 in clicks. Writers stopped opening ChatGPT. The design system was picked up by three sister products.

impact.headline: Reflection
wentWell: The one-page flow tested well from round one. The simplest bet was the right one.
AI in the canvas landed because it stayed the writer's tool: assist, not automate.
The design system got real adoption. That was as important as the two flows.
differently: I would run the first user session earlier. Two of the audit findings were validated in fifteen minutes.
I would treat the micro-copy pass as its own round from the start. It saved us more time in build than any layout change did.
